item.title: More choices for test centres among key changes for NEET (PG) 2026
item.description: The reforms are aimed at making the process more convenient for the candidates, according to the Union Health Ministry; a total of 2,73,183 candidates have registered for NEET (PG) 2026 which will be conducted in a single shift across around 340 cities and more than 1,300 examination centres

item.title: Sasikala, others booked over DYFI leader’s complaint
item.description: The accused reportedly circulated a video of the complainant and her friends, captioning it “MDMA comrades” and adding provocative remarks

item.title: MVD cracks down on erring bike riders in Kochi
item.description: Of the 80 vehicles inspected, 35 had banned silencers, while 20 had other violations

item.title: Call grows louder for new water tank at Thammanam in Kochi
item.description: The new tank at Thammanam was proposed following the partial collapse of the 1.35-crore-litre water tank, which had triggered a temporary drinking water crisis in the city

item.title: Health Minister inaugurates development projects at Ernakulam General Hospital
item.description: Minister inaugurates a tensile-roof walkway, a yard development and drainage project, and the Gastroenterology department at the General Hospital

item.description: The IMD had warned fishers against venturing out into the sea off Kerala, Karnataka, and Lakshadweep in view of possible gusty winds and inclement weather

item.title: Incessant downpour disrupts life in Kerala’s Kozhikode
item.description: Eight relief camps opened in district accommodating 214 persons from 72 families evacuated from vulnerable areas

item.title: Heavy rain batters Kerala’s Kannur, two missing, 26 shifted to relief camp
item.description: Eight families comprising 26 people were shifted to a relief camp after floodwaters entered houses at Peratta Thottipalam in Ulikkal grama panchayat

item.title: The hopes of two families are dashed as terror attack leaves their sole breadwinners dead
item.description: Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai announces an ex gratiaassistance of ₹20 lakh each for the families of the two Chhattisgarh workers killed in a terror attack in Kelam area of south Kashmir’s Kulgam district late on Friday evening

item.title: DMK to boycott verification of EVMs in Kolathur alleging lapses; plans to go to court

item.description: “This is not re-counting. This is EVM Checking and Verification process,” Chennai District Election Officer and Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said. “It is a 100% transparent exercise to establish the reliability of the EVMs.”

item.title: NEET-UG counselling to begin on August 4, academic session from September 8
item.description: According to the counselling schedule released by the committee, the first round of AIQ counselling for deemed and central universities will be held from August 4 to August 17. The last date for joining will be August 22

item.title: Protection for certain royal estates from succession law still valid despite abolition of privy purses and privileges: Karnataka High Court
item.description: The court holds that while the purport and object of the Gaddi or ceremonial throne has lost its relevance, from the customary practical perspective, it is still a relevant subject

item.title: Amrutanjan pays rental arrears on temple property

item.description: Satheesan reportedly flew aboard the helicopter from Thiruvananthapuram to Kochi to visit his father-in-law, who was undergoing treatment. As Leader of the Opposition, he had criticised the then LDF government for its “extravagance” in hiring the helicopter.

item.title: Telugu language, culture take centre stage at ATA conference in the United States
Why fishers in Kerala ignore dire warnings and venture into sea
item.description: For many fisher families, heightened risk at sea remains secondary to the immediate threat of starvation on land. Government issues ‘stay-at-home’ directives in extreme weather conditions, but no minimum wages or guaranteed compensation is offered, leaving the fishers shorn of livelihood, say their union leaders

item.title: ‘Every effort being made to maximise Godavari waters for farmers’ benefit’
item.description: Irrigation Minister Uttam Kumar along with Cabinet colleagues Sridhar Babu, Vivek and Laxman Kumar reviews inflows into projects; says landmark projects built during Congress regimes continue to serve the State and rejects claims that water pumped from Yellampalli was Kaleshwaram water

item.title: Kerala floods 2026: Landslips, overflowing rivers leave trail of destruction in Kerala’s Kottayam
item.description: Three persons, including an 11-year-old boy, dead. 26 relief camps, including six in Kanjirappally taluk, were opened across the district, providing shelter to 567 people

item.title: Tamil Nadu native arrested for running fake online Kerala lottery racket
item.description: According to police, he created websites designed to resemble official Kerala government lottery portal by using Kerala Lotteries name, official logos and government address to mislead customers

item.title: Kerala floods 2026: Pathanamthitta reels under floods as torrential rain pounds district
item.description: Ranni emerged as the worst-affected area, with the town virtually cut off after floodwaters submerged key approach roads, including the Ranni-Vadasserikkara road, bringing traffic to a standstill. The town remained under two to two-and-a-half feet of water through the day

item.title: Marble statue of Swami Vivekananda presented to Modi

item.title: Over 3,000 serving CAPF officers move Supreme Court against CAPF Act

item.title: Antilia bomb scare: Charges framed; ex-cops Waze, Sharma & eight others to face trial for murder
item.description: The accused will face trial for offences under the Indian Penal Code related to murder, extortion, destruction of evidence and criminal conspiracy, as well as under relevant provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and the Explosive Substances Act

item.title: On Kore’s 79th birthday leaders hail his contribution to north Karnataka
item.description: Member of Parliament and Former Chief Minister Jagadish Shettar said that Padma Shri awardee Prabhakar Kore’s contributions to the fields of education, healthcare, cooperation and industry over the past four decades had played a significant role in the development of North Karnataka.

item.title: Tapal Ganesh seeks fresh CEC review of Ballari lease categorisation

item.title: TISS postpones convocation with CJI as chief guest; students on visit for ceremony affected
item.description: In an email to students on Friday, the institute said the decision was taken under “unforeseen circumstances” and in the “best long-term interests of the institute”. Affected students say they spent on non-refundable flight and train tickets and hotel bookings.

item.title: Forum stages protest seeking clearance for Kalasa-Banduri drinking water project in Hubballi
item.description: Condemning what they termed as stepmotherly treatment of Karnataka by the Union government, members of the Mahadayi Kalasa-Banduri Horata Samiti staged a protest outside Union Minister Pralhad Joshi’s office in Hubballi on Saturday and courted arrest

item.title: U.P. moving towards police state, violence being normalised, say retired cops
item.description: The government is making the police uncivilized, says retired IPS officer of U.P. cadre Vibhuti Narain Rai while former DGP Sulkhan Singh points out that the State is normalising violence leading to an environment where society accepts such violent actions as a form of ‘instant justice’

item.title: DMK moves Supreme Court to direct Karnataka to release Tamil Nadu’s share of Cauvery water
item.description: The application asks Karnataka to ensure a flow of 3,500 cusecs per day at the inter-State contact point at Biligundlu in line with the July 28 direction of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee

item.title: Keep visiting Kolkata, your safety is my responsibility, West Bengal CM tells Taslima
item.description: Taslima Nasrin said that it was her dream to return to Kolkata and “history will remember those who shut the door on her and those who opened the door”

item.title: Varanasi police book MPs Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav and Awadesh Prasad for 'insulting Sanatan Dharma'
